To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The processing of emotional words is sensitive to task demands.
The processing of emotional words depends on the type of task.
the effects of emotional content are found when a lexico- semantic analysis is necessary, and that these effects are found in a late positivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the processing of affective information in the context of word processing.
the question of whether the processing of emotional words is sensitive to task requirements and whether this sensitivity can be revealed by means of electrophysiological measures.
the processing of emotional stimuli in a non-emotional task.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the processing of emotion words is influenced by task demands and that the emotional content of words is processed differently depending on the task.
the affective content of words is processed differently, depending on task requirements, but the affective content can be detected even when it is not the task requirement.
the allocation of resources to the emotional content of words depends on task demands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the emotional content is only processed when the task requires a semantic analysis.
the affective meaning of a word can be accessed at different levels of word processing.
the affective content is not automatically processed, and that this is reflected by the absence of effects in task 1 and the occurrence of effects in task2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the processing of emotional words is modulated by task instructions.
the processing of emotional information during word processing is task dependent.
the allocation of resources to emotional content in word processing is sensitive to task demands and that some level of semantic analysis is required to detect the emotional content of words.
